sources.name: Greenhouse Job Board API
sources.rateLimit: No limit is documented for the Job Board API (absent from the official docs source, grnhse/greenhouse-api-docs). Self-impose 1 request/second and cache each board for 24 h. Greenhouse's customer MSA (customer-facing, not specific to this API) bars 'excessive or abusive' API use and lets Greenhouse throttle or suspend.
sources.attribution: None stated in the docs.
fields: single job only: company_name, first_published, application_deadline, pay_input_ranges (pay_transparency=true), questions (questions=true), data_compliance
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint exists (the docs list none). The board_token is the 'Job Board URL token', i.e. the last path segment of a company's Greenhouse-hosted board URL, and appears in embed/iframe and ?gh_jid links on the company's own careers page (Greenhouse support article 'Find your job board URL': https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155-Find-your-job-board-URL). Lawful prospect list: start from companies found via other lawful sources (HN hiring threads, aggregator feeds, trade press, registers); open each company's own public careers page once; record the token only if that page links to Greenhouse; never brute-force or dictionary-guess tokens; honour robots.txt on the careers page.
sources.notes: Verified on the official docs source: 'Job Board data is publicly available, so authentication is not required for any GET endpoints.' Other GET endpoints: /v1/boards/{token} (name, content), /jobs/{job_id}, /departments, /offices, /sections, /educations (render_as=list|tree). Only the application POST needs Basic Auth - never call it. The docs state no terms of use, so treat output as internal prospecting data: keep company, title, location, URL, dates; do not republish employer job descriptions (copyright stays with the employer). Freshness: live, reflects currently published posts. Coverage: only companies running a Greenhouse board. updated_at is last-edit time, not posting date. Sample: samples/greenhouse-board.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Lever Postings API
sources.rateLimit: No GET limit documented. The README documents a limit only for application POSTs (2 per second, HTTP 429) and says it 'may also be changed without warning'. Self-impose 1 request/second and cache 24 h.
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: createdAt (unverified: not in the README field table)
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. README: 'Each company currently only has one site (usually your company name with no spaces)'; the site name is the path segment of the company's Lever-hosted postings page (host jobs.lever.co - unverified this session) or of links on its own careers page. EU-hosted accounts use https://api.eu.lever.co/v0/postings/{site}. Lawful prospect list: same method as Greenhouse - take the site name only from links the company itself publishes; do not guess names.
sources.notes: Verified in README: GET list '/v0/postings/SITE?skip=X&limit=Y', single '/v0/postings/SITE/POSTING-ID', params mode (json|html|iframe), skip, limit, location, commitment, team, department, level, group. README sentences: 'Note that all job postings in the published state are publicly viewable', 'These jobs may be scraped by third parties' and 'All other jobs are completely hidden from the jobs API' - the clearest third-party-access statement of the ATS vendors, but it is not a licence. JSON is chosen with '&mode=json' or an 'Accept: application/json' header; the README says 'In JSON mode, each job posting is a JSON object with the following fields' and does not state whether the list is a bare array (assumed) or wrapped; the group parameter changes the output shape (not described); skip/limit defaults and maximums are not stated. Lever's Terms of Service bind customers, not readers of public postings. Never use the POST apply endpoint (needs a customer API key). Freshness: live. Sample: samples/lever-postings.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Ashby Public Job Posting API
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Self-impose 1 request/second and cache 24 h.
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: jobs[].address.postalAddress (locality, region, country; exact key spelling unverified)
compensation (compensationTierSummary, scrapeableCompensationSalarySummary, compensationTiers, summaryComponents; only if includeCompensation=true; docs conflict on top-level vs per-job placement)
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint documented. The job board name is the last segment of the hosted board URL, e.g. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/Ashby -> 'Ashby' (docs). Lawful prospect list: take the name only from links on the company's own careers page or from job URLs the company published (e.g. in an HN hiring post); never guess names.
sources.notes: The docs page shows an unauthenticated curl example but does not say 'no authentication' in words (inference; confirm with the first live test). Respect jobs[].isListed: if false the posting should only be reachable by direct link, so do not list or store it. Ashby's Customer Terms (5.1) restrict customers, say nothing about third parties reading the public feed. Missing data stays missing (for example an empty country). Freshness: live. Sample: samples/ashby-posting-api.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: SmartRecruiters Posting API (public postings)
sources.rateLimit: Customer API throttling policy per developer docs (https://developers.smartrecruiters.com/docs/rate-limiting): 10 requests/second and 8 concurrent, HTTP 429 when exceeded. Whether that applies to unauthenticated Posting API calls is unverified. Self-impose 1 request/second.
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: content[].location (country, region, city, remote, latitude, longitude)
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. companyIdentifier is the path segment after https://careers.smartrecruiters.com/ on the company's hosted careers page (docs). Lawful prospect list: take it only from links the company publishes (careers page, job URLs). Paging: limit max 100, offset.
sources.notes: Documentation conflict, flagged: the older Customer API overview lists the Posting API under endpoints available 'Without Authentication', while other pages say the Public Posting API supports API key or OAuth 2.0 client credentials. The list endpoint has a destination parameter; use PUBLIC (INTERNAL needs an OAuth scope you will not have). No developer or API terms for the Posting API were found (search summary), only customer terms. Freshness: live; releasedDate is the publish date. Sample: samples/smartrecruiters-posting.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Workable public account jobs endpoint
sources.rateLimit: Not documented for this public endpoint. The authenticated API is limited to 10 requests per 10 seconds per account token (https://workable.readme.io/reference/rate-limits). Self-impose 1 request/second.
sources.attribution: None stated.
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. 'subdomain' is the first part of the company's Workable URL; for a prospect, take it from the link on its own careers page (apply.workable.com/{subdomain}/ pattern - unverified this session). Companion public endpoints: /api/accounts/{subdomain}/locations and /departments (docs titles).
sources.notes: Documented as returning 'a collection of the public jobs for an account'. Doc inconsistencies flagged: the accounts reference describes url as the application form and application_url as the job page, the /jobs reference and sample say the opposite; telecommuting is top-level in one place and nested under location in another. Workable says its API is mostly server-to-server and points browser users to JSONP for public job info. Do not use the authenticated /spi/v3 API (needs the customer's token). Freshness: live at request time; coverage limited to Workable customers whose subdomain you lawfully learn. Top-level wrapper keys of the response (name, description, jobs) are unverified. Sample: samples/workable-public.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Recruitee Careers Site API
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Self-impose 1 request/second and cache 24 h.
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: screening questions (documented as part of GET /offers when configured)
id, slug, title, description, requirements, location, city, country, department, tags, employment_type_code, remote, published_at (all unverified: not confirmed on a doc page this session)
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. {company} is the subdomain of the company's Recruitee careers site (Settings > Company settings > Careers site, per docs). Lawful prospect list: take the subdomain from the company's own careers page link. XML variants exist (/api/offers.xml and /api/feeds/offers.xml per the Recruitee support FAQ https://support.recruitee.com/en/articles/8213076-faq-api).
sources.notes: Only the public Careers Site API is in scope. The Core API at api.recruitee.com/c/{company_id}/... needs a bearer token generated in a customer account - not available to us. No separate API terms found; termsUrl points at the docs getting-started page for lack of anything better (unverified). Freshness: live at request time; coverage limited to Recruitee customers. Recruitee docs describe themselves as a work in progress and the search-summary sample JSON looked like test data, so treat the field list as provisional until a first live call. Sample: samples/recruitee-careers.json (field names beyond careers_url/careers_apply_url are unverified).

sources.name: Personio XML job feed
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Feed updates automatically when the customer edits a job (Personio FAQ). Self-impose 1 request per host per day for lead generation.
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: root element name, createdAt, keywords, occupation (all unverified)
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. The feed lives on the customer's own Personio career-site host with /xml appended; language values de, en, fr, es, nl, it, pt (docs). Host variants (.jobs.personio.de vs .jobs.personio.com) vary by account (unverified) - read the careers page link. Strong in German and wider EU SMEs. Lawful prospect list: from careers-page links only.
sources.notes: Verified (Personio FAQ summary): 'You don't need credentials'; legal entities have no separate feed (filter the parent feed by subcompany); defaults to German unless language=en. Format is XML, not JSON (sample file wraps the XML in a JSON string). Forum posts report CORS errors in browsers (server-side fetch is fine) and that custom application-form attributes are not in the feed. Personio's separate Recruiting API needs customer credentials - out of scope. Sample: samples/personio-xml.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Teamtailor public jobs RSS feed
sources.rateLimit: Not documented. Default 100 jobs per feed; use offset and per_page URL parameters to page (docs). Self-impose 1 request per host per day.
sources.attribution: None stated.
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. Take a Teamtailor-built careers site's main jobs page and add '.rss' (docs example: https://career.teamtailor.com/jobs.rss). Custom domains work the same way (jobs page URL + .rss). Lawful prospect list: from the company's own careers page.
sources.notes: The Teamtailor REST API (api.teamtailor.com for EU, api.na.teamtailor.com for NA) needs an API key that only a Company Admin of the customer account can generate - not available to us and not a lead source. The RSS guide says the feed shows publicly available data only. Freshness: live at request time; coverage limited to Teamtailor-built careers sites. The guide lists data points; the RSS element names are unverified, so the sample uses standard RSS 2.0 elements plus placeholders. Sample: samples/teamtailor-rss.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: Pinpoint Job Postings JSON endpoint
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Self-impose 1 request per host per day.
sources.attribution: None stated.
sources.discovery: No enumeration endpoint. {company-subdomain} is the customer's Pinpoint careers-site subdomain; locale prefix possible (https://workwithus.pinpointhq.com/fr/postings.json). Filters documented by example: department and division IDs, location_city_state_name=London,Warsaw. Lawful prospect list: from careers-page links only.
sources.notes: Documented as replacing jobs.json; the 'Job Feeds Overview' page still lists /jobs.json and /jobs.xml, so the docs disagree on the older feeds - prefer postings.json. Docs say it can be fetched client-side with no CORS issues. Freshness: live at request time; coverage limited to Pinpoint customers. No terms page found (unverified). The sample uses key names inferred from the prose field list and is flagged as shape-unverified. Sample: samples/pinpoint-json.json.

sources.name: BambooHR careers list and ATS API
sources.rateLimit: Not applicable (documented API needs customer credentials).
sources.attribution: n/a
fields: documented ATS job summaries only (customer credentials required)
sources.discovery: n/a. The documented endpoint GET /api/v1/applicant_tracking/jobs needs OAuth scope hiring:applications and ATS-settings access in a customer account. A public per-company careers JSON list is widely reported by developers but is NOT documented by BambooHR (unverified here), so it is excluded.
sources.notes: Searches of the official documentation found no public, unauthenticated job feed. Building on an undocumented endpoint risks breaking terms and breaking silently. Revisit only if BambooHR publishes a public careers feed in its docs. Company careers pages hosted on BambooHR can still be read one at a time by a human like any web page.

sources.name: JazzHR API and XML job feed
sources.rateLimit: Not documented in the pages found. XML feed is a static file cached for 24 hours (JazzHR help center).
sources.attribution: n/a
fields: GET /jobs returns a JSON array (job records without url/buttons); board_code is used to build apply links
sources.discovery: n/a. The 32-character API key sits on the customer's Settings > Integrations tab and is visible only to Super Administrators, Recruiting Administrators or Developers; the XML feed is found under Settings > Career Page > XML FEED in the customer's own account. Neither is obtainable for other companies.
sources.notes: Only usable for a client that hands Amber its own key or feed URL, which is a service-delivery integration, not lead generation. Not a source for prospecting.

sources.name: Breezy HR API
sources.rateLimit: Not documented in the pages found; page size capped at 50 when paginating.
sources.attribution: n/a
fields: documented v3 positions endpoint returns the token-holder's own company positions (authenticated)
sources.discovery: n/a. No documented public, unauthenticated careers JSON feed was found in Breezy's developer documentation; a public '/json' careers feed is sometimes mentioned by developers but is undocumented (unverified), so it is excluded.
sources.notes: A token gives access only to the token-holder's own company data, so it cannot see other employers. Revisit if Breezy documents a public feed.

sources.name: Hacker News Firebase API ('Ask HN: Who is hiring?' threads)
sources.rateLimit: README: 'There is currently no rate limit.' Be polite anyway: 2-5 requests/second. Each comment is a separate item fetch (kids[] list), so a thread of several hundred comments is several hundred requests; fetch once a month and cache.
sources.attribution: None stated; credit Hacker News when quoting.
sources.discovery: The monthly hiring thread is a story titled 'Ask HN: Who is hiring? (Month YYYY)'; seen this session: October 2026 = item 49922569, September 2026 = 49522897, August 2026 = 49156683 (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49922569). Newest thread: look up the HN account that posts them (believed to be 'whoishiring', unverified in the README) via /v0/user/{id}.json and read its submitted list (field assumed, unverified), or find the id with the Algolia API. Top-level comments (kids[] of the story) are the job posts; replies are noise. Extract company name, role, location, remote flag and public URLs. Job URLs to known ATS hosts (boards.greenhouse.io, jobs.lever.co, jobs.ashbyhq.com, apply.workable.com, careers.smartrecruiters.com) reveal ATS tokens the company itself published.
sources.notes: Best self-seeding employer source: no key, no stated limit, employers publish their own hiring signal. PERSONAL DATA WARNING: each post is written by an individual and often includes their email address; do not extract or store emails or names; keep company, role, location, public URLs, thread id and comment id (provenance). Do not ingest 'Ask HN: Who wants to be hired?' (exists for October 2026, item 49922568) or 'Freelancer? Seeking freelancer?' threads: they are about individuals. The README is MIT-licensed documentation, not a data licence; HN's own terms of use were not verified this session (search budget exhausted) - owner should read them once. Freshness: threads appear monthly and fill over days. Sample: samples/hn-firebase.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: HN Search API (Algolia) for hiring threads
sources.rateLimit: Docs: requests from one IP are capped at 10,000 per hour (repeated in the node-hacker-news-api README). A query returns at most 1,000 hits whatever the page value (GitHub issues algolia/hn-search #125 and #230); slice by created_at_i windows. hitsPerPage accepts 1 to 1000 per that client's README and a maintainer comment in #125 (not in the docs parameter table).
sources.attribution: None stated.
fields: hits[] (item field names unverified this session: objectID, author, title, comment_text, created_at, created_at_i, story_id, parent_id, points, url)
wrapper keys seen in a GitHub issue transcript: hits, nbHits, page, nbPages, hitsPerPage, exhaustiveNbHits, exhaustiveTypo, query, params, processingTimeMS
request params: query, tags, numericFilters, page, hitsPerPage (hitsPerPage=100 used in a GitHub issue; not in the docs parameter table)
documented tags: story, comment, poll, pollopt, show_hn, ask_hn, front_page, author_:USERNAME, story_:ID
documented numeric filters: created_at_i, points, num_comments
sources.discovery: Use it only to find the thread id: tags=story,author_whoishiring on search_by_date (author tag form 'author_:USERNAME' is in the docs; the exact literal usage and the author name are unverified - test once), then page the comments with tags=comment,story_{id} or switch to the Firebase API for the comment bodies.
sources.notes: Docs state tags are ANDed by default and parentheses OR them, e.g. author_pg,(story,poll). The docs page is old (about 3,100 days per search metadata), so confirm behaviour on first call. Same personal-data rules as hn-firebase. Sample: samples/hn-algolia.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested; hit field names unverified).

sources.name: Remote OK jobs API
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Poll at most a few times a day and cache.
sources.attribution: ToS (search summary of remoteok.com/legal): 'You agree to link back with a web hyperlink or in-app hyperlink to our site on the page or app screen where you use the data from our APIs or site.' Feed notice quoted in the Ruby client README: 'Please link back to the URL on Remote OK and mention Remote OK as a source, so we get traffic back from your site.' and 'If you do not we'll have to suspend API access.' Fuller notice quoted in a third-party README ('Legal notice from the Remote ok API'): 'By using Remote OK's API feed you legally agree to mention Remote OK as a source' and 'link back to the job listing URL on Remote OK with a DIRECT link, no redirects please.' A third-party CLI README adds that the API Terms require a follow backlink (no nofollow) - unverified. FAQ: credit Remote OK and link to each original job post URL. Do not use the logo without written permission.
fields: first array element is a legal-notice object (reported by clients, unverified)
sources.discovery: The feed lists employers directly (company, logo, job URL). It does not reveal ATS tokens (url and apply_url point back to Remote OK).
sources.notes: Low-risk use: internal lead research with the attribution kept in each record; do not republish listings or strip the link back. The API has no separate schema page; the field list comes from a third-party client README, so the shape is provisional. Freshness: live board. A third-party CLI README says Remote OK returns 403 to default or bot User-Agents and needs 'no account or token' (unverified): use an honest User-Agent and, if blocked with 403, stop and drop the source or ask Remote OK - do not spoof a browser. Sample: samples/remoteok-api.json (documentation-derived from the client README, not live-tested).

sources.name: Remotive remote jobs API
sources.rateLimit: README: 'we advise max. 4 times a day'; 'excessive requests (more than 2x per minute) will be blocked'; jobs are delayed by 24 hours.
sources.attribution: README: 'Please link back to the URL found on Remotive AND mention Remotive as a source'; 'If you don't do that, we'll terminate your API access'. Do not submit Remotive jobs to third-party sites (README names Jooble, Neuvoo, Google Jobs, LinkedIn Jobs). Displaying jobs to collect signups or email addresses 'constitutes a breach of our terms of services'. Private paid API: hello(at)remotive(dot)com.
sources.discovery: Filters: category (slug, list at /api/remote-jobs/categories), company_name (case-insensitive partial), search, limit. Feed lists employers directly; url points to Remotive, not to an ATS.
sources.notes: The 'Terms of Services' heading in the README is not linked to a separate page. Use for internal prospecting only, keep the Remotive URL in the record, never feed it into another board or into outreach copy that republishes the listing. Freshness: 24 h delayed by design. Sample: samples/remotive-api.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: We Work Remotely RSS feeds
sources.rateLimit: Not documented. Poll once or twice a day.
sources.attribution: Feed page (search summary): anyone can use the feed; 'all we ask is that you attribute the links back to We Work Remotely'.
fields: standard RSS 2.0 item elements (title, link, guid, pubDate, description) - unverified; WWR-specific elements unverified
sources.discovery: Main feed: weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss; per-category feeds exist under weworkremotely.com/categories/ (Customer Support, Product, Full-Stack/Back-End/Front-End/All Programming, Sales and Marketing, Management and Finance, Design, DevOps and SysAdmin, All Other). Employer name is usually in the item title.
sources.notes: The general Terms and Conditions (updated July 20, 2026 per search metadata) concern user-uploaded content; they do not address feed readers. The separate API terms do NOT apply to the RSS feed (see wwr-api). Coverage: remote jobs posted to WWR only; freshness: as posted (update interval not documented). Sample: samples/wwr-rss.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested; elements provisional).

sources.name: We Work Remotely READ API
sources.rateLimit: API page says up to 1,000 requests per day per authenticated user, but the page is old (about 1,350 days) and its 429 text mentions a monthly quota; unreliable.
sources.attribution: Terms list attribution; applicants must be sent through the WWR website.
sources.discovery: n/a. How to obtain a token could not be verified.
sources.notes: Search summary of the terms: commercial use is permitted if you do not build something meant to harm, compete with or replace WWR; only data exposed through the API may be used; 'scraping, copying, saving, or storing our data is strictly prohibited'. Storing listings in a prospect database conflicts with that, so use the public RSS feed instead (wwr-rss) and leave this API.

sources.name: Arbeitnow Job Board API
sources.rateLimit: Not documented (unverified). Poll a few times a day.
sources.attribution: Terms section 11 (search summary): users of the API agree to provide a link back to Arbeitnow.com on their platform; Arbeitnow may revoke permission at any time; API provided 'as is'.
fields: query params: search, location, page (third-party OpenAPI spec); visa_sponsorship=true|false (Arbeitnow blog via search summary)
sources.discovery: Feed lists employers directly. Jobs are largely aggregated from ATS platforms (Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, Join.com, Teamtailor, Recruitee, Comeet - Arbeitnow blog), mostly Germany and wider Europe, so it is a good way to find European employers; the url points to Arbeitnow, so ATS tokens must be learned from each company's own careers page.
sources.notes: Free API needs no key; a paid private endpoint exists. Arbeitnow's own docs page was not readable this session; the field list above comes from a third-party OpenAPI spec generated for an unofficial SDK (github.com/voxgig-sdk/arbeitnow-sdk, .sdk/def/arbeitnow_0.1.0.json: server https://www.arbeitnow.com/api, GET /job-board-api), so treat it as provisional until the first live call. A UK mirror domain (arbeitnow.co.uk) was mentioned by the blog (unverified). Visa-sponsorship filter is useful for international-placement targeting. Coverage: Germany and wider Europe; freshness: live board. Sample: samples/arbeitnow-api.json (documentation-derived via the third-party spec, not live-tested).

sources.name: Himalayas Remote Jobs API
sources.rateLimit: README: 'The API is rate limited to keep it fast and available for everyone'; exceeding it returns 429; 'We don't publish an exact number'; data is 'cached and refreshed every 24 hours' so 'polling more often than once per day gains you nothing'. Browse feed: limit default 20, max 20, offset default 0. Higher limits by emailing hi@himalayas.app (site docs, via search summary).
sources.attribution: README, section 'Attribution and terms of use': 'The API is free to use, including commercially.' Link back to each job's URL on himalayas.app (use the applicationLink or guid field) and 'Credit Himalayas as the source of the data wherever you display it.' 'Do not resubmit' Himalayas listings to third-party job aggregators, 'including but not limited to Jooble, Neuvoo, Google Jobs, and LinkedIn Jobs'. The repository's example code is MIT; the job data is not, it falls under the attribution terms. The general site terms (https://himalayas.app/terms) bar copying or distributing information from the services and reselling or monetizing related data without consent (search summary).
fields: envelope: comments, updatedAt, offset, limit, totalCount, jobs
search endpoint params: q, country, worldwide, exclude_worldwide, seniority, employment_type, company (companySlug), timezone, sort, page
sources.discovery: Feed lists employers directly (companyName, companySlug, companyLogo). Two endpoints: browse GET https://himalayas.app/jobs/api and filtered GET https://himalayas.app/jobs/api/search. Alternative: RSS of the 100 newest jobs at https://himalayas.app/jobs/rss (repo himalayas-app/remote-jobs-rss-feed: also cached 24 hours; item elements title, description, link, guid, pubDate, category, content:encoded, media:content plus himalayasJobs:companyName / companyLogo / locationRestriction / timezoneRestriction / expiryDate).
sources.notes: Best-documented aggregator: official GitHub README with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec (openapi.json and openapi.yaml in the repo; hosted copy https://himalayas.app/docs/openapi.json, not fetched). Docs conflict, flagged: the README documents limit/offset while the site docs page (search summary) says cursor pagination is preferred and offset is deprecated - check the OpenAPI spec on the first call. Employer-side use for an internal prospect dashboard fits the allowed uses the site docs list (populate internal dashboards). About 95,000 listings per the org's repo description. Sample: samples/himalayas-api.json (documentation-derived from the README field list, not live-tested; value formats invented).

sources.name: Jobicy Remote Jobs API
sources.rateLimit: README: 'Automated polling must not run more frequently than once per hour'; respect HTTP 429 and Retry-After; no numeric request cap. count 1-200 per call (default 200); cursor pagination; listings from the last 7 days.
sources.attribution: README Fair Use: 'Keep Jobicy as the original source and preserve the canonical Jobicy job URL when displaying a listing.' 'Do not present Jobicy listings as your own original job postings or remove source attribution.' 'Do not use Jobicy data to create spam networks, misleading job databases, or services that negatively affect employers, candidates, or platform stability.' You 'may use Jobicy listings in your own products and user experiences without requesting individual permission.' 'Normal integrations do not require a separate agreement.'
sources.discovery: Feed lists employers directly. Filters: geo, industry, tag, plus ?get=locations and ?get=industries taxonomies. Optional paid key (USD 0.01 per job once per key) returns the original ATS application URL in url - not recommended at a $0 budget.
sources.notes: Clearest permission text of the aggregators. Caution: the 'negatively affect employers' clause means outreach must be low volume, individually owner-reviewed, and must never quote or repost the listing. Status check: HEAD on the Jobicy vacancy URL, 404/410 = no longer active. Repository code is MIT; the licence does not cover listings or logos. Official OpenAPI at https://jobicy.com/api/openapi.json (not fetched). Sample: samples/jobicy-api.json (documentation-derived, not live-tested).

sources.name: The Muse Jobs API v2
sources.rateLimit: Docs: 500 requests/hour without a key, 3,600 requests/hour with api_key; headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset; HTTP 403 when exceeded. The older docs say registration is required for any use beyond testing.
sources.attribution: No attribution requirement found (not on the docs page). API terms: licence is 'limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, and revocable' to build and distribute Apps; no replicating The Muse's products; comply with rate limits.
fields: job fields unverified: name, type, publication_date, short_name, model_type, id, contents, locations, categories, levels, tags, refs, company
sources.discovery: Endpoints /jobs, /jobs/{id}, /companies, /companies/{id}; filters page (required), category, level, company, location, descending. Company profiles help rank mid-size and large employers.
sources.notes: Owner action: register for a free key on the developer page (a signup only the owner may do) and read the API terms once; use is internal prospecting, not building an app. The docs page and terms are old (about 3,900 days per search metadata). Job field names could not be confirmed from the docs this session; the sample is flagged shape-unverified. Sample: samples/themuse-api.json.

sources.name: Adzuna API
sources.rateLimit: Terms page: default 25 hits/minute, 250/day, 1,000/week, 2,500/month; Adzuna may vary them and will raise them 'where there is mutual commercial benefit'.
sources.attribution: Each displayed ad must carry an 'Adzuna' label hyperlinked to the country domain; research uses must credit 'The Adzuna API' and link to the Adzuna site.

sources.rateLimit: Static monthly snapshot: ZIP files of CSV (several parts), compiled to the end of the previous month and available within 5 working days of month end. fields: mortgage charge counts (CSV column headers unverified)
sources.discovery: Filter status Active and SIC 78200 (Temporary employment agency activities) and 78109 (Other activities of employment placement agencies) to list UK recruitment and staffing companies; 78300 (Human resources provision and management of human resources functions) is a weaker signal. Many recruitment firms carry two or three of these codes. The same file resolves any UK employer by name or number. SIC labels verified in Companies House's own enumerations repo (github.com/companieshouse/api-enumerations, constants.yml): 78109 'Other activities of employment placement agencies', 78200 'Temporary employment agency activities', 78300 'Human resources provision and management of human resources functions'; 78101 is 'Motion picture, television and other theatrical casting activities' (a casting code, ignore).
sources.notes: Best scalable agency list found: company-level data only, no officers. Caveats: SIC codes are self-declared and some companies have none; an older FOI response says SIC may be missing in a company's first year (may no longer apply); registered offices of micro-companies can be a director's home address, so never use addresses for marketing - find the company website and a role-based address instead; sole traders and many partnerships are not on this register (the ICO treats them as individual subscribers). sources.name: Common Crawl (index and archives)
sources.rateLimit: Not published in the pages seen. Archives sit on Amazon S3 (bucket 'commoncrawl', prefix crawl-data/CC-MAIN-...), but the cc-index-server README (github.com/commoncrawl/cc-index-server) says access to the data through the S3 API is restricted to authenticated AWS users - an AWS account would be an owner signup; anonymous HTTPS access is recalled but unverified. The index server takes a collection name plus url= (README example: .../CC-MAIN-2015-06-index?url=commoncrawl.org); prefix/domain matching and output=json are documented in pywb's CDX Server API wiki (github.com/webrecorder/pywb/wiki/CDX-Server-API): url, matchType = exact|prefix|host|domain, output=json, limit, fl, from, to, filter, page, showNumPages; record fields urlkey, timestamp, url, mime, status, digest, length, offset, filename. That Common Crawl's public index server accepts the same parameters is inferred from its pywb-based README and unverified.
sources.attribution: Terms (search summary): crawled content may carry separate terms from its owners; users agree to respect third-party copyrights; Common Crawl recommends legal advice before any use, including commercial; the terms prohibit collecting or harvesting personally identifiable information for use separately from the crawled content.
fields: URL index records (urlkey, timestamp, url, status, mime - names unverified)
sources.discovery: Method: query the URL index for prefixes of ATS hosts (boards.greenhouse.io/*, jobs.lever.co/*, jobs.ashbyhq.com/*) to learn which tokens exist without touching the vendor - a lawful way to build a token list from a public archive; or search crawled careers pages for JobPosting JSON-LD. The URL-index query syntax is documented (pywb); applying it to Common Crawl's public server, and the JobPosting search, are unverified procedures.
sources.notes: Free but engineering-heavy, stale by weeks to months, and the terms push legal responsibility onto the user, with an explicit PII-harvesting ban. Not worth building first. If used, keep to company-level facts (company name, role title, URL) and never store names or emails found in pages. CCBot honours robots.txt and a site can opt out, so archive coverage excludes sites that blocked it.

sources.name: schema.org JobPosting on a company's own careers pages
sources.rateLimit: Method, not an API: fetch one careers page per company per week at most, identify yourself in the User-Agent, obey robots.txt and any crawl-delay, never log in or bypass a block.

Stay on the employer's own domain; never use it to read aggregator pages whose terms ban scraping. Page-by-page, owner-reviewed volume only. Sample: samples/schema-org-jobposting.json (built from the required properties in Google's documentation; not a copy of any real page).

sources.name: Agency and employer own websites (contact and careers pages)
sources.rateLimit: Method: one visit per page, sequential, identified User-Agent, obey robots.txt.
sources.attribution: Each site's own terms apply; read contact and careers pages the way a browser would, respect robots.txt, and record only what the company publishes for business enquiries.
fields: published role-based email (e.g. info@, hello@, jobs@, partnerships@)
sources.discovery: Take the company website from Companies House, SEC, the sponsor register or an aggregator listing; open its Contact, Careers, Partners or Work-with-us page; record only what the company itself publishes for business enquiries.
sources.notes: Lawful contact channels, in order: (1) published contact or partnership form, filled in by the owner by hand; (2) role-based address published for business or recruitment enquiries; (3) a postal address. FTC (CAN-SPAM): no business-to-business exemption; no opt-in needed in the US but every message needs accurate headers, a non-deceptive subject, a valid postal address and a working opt-out honoured within 10 business days. ICO: PECR email rules do not require consent for corporate subscribers (companies, LLPs) but sole traders and some partnerships count as individuals; when unsure treat as individual. Several EU states are stricter (Germany is the usual example - unverified here); take advice before EU outreach. Never guess personal addresses, never use email finders, never copy emails out of job posts. Sample: samples/agency-company-websites.json.
